chunks: if you endure even then matters will move on as ordained by Allāh but in that case you will deserve reward; while if you lose patience, matters will again move as ordained by Allāh, but in this case you will be bearing the burden (of sins).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between being ma'jur and ma'zoor in the context of divine decree?
ai.summary: In this concise address to Ash‘ath, Imam Ali (AS) highlights the Shia theological nuance that while divine decree (al-Qadar) is inevitable, human agency determines whether one becomes a recipient of reward or a bearer of sin. This distinction underscores the practical implication of *sabr* (patience) not merely as passive endurance, but as an active spiritual state that transforms trial into merit, a concept central to Nahj al-Balagha’s ethical teachings.
